summary: The agent juggles four systems in one session — retail store-purchases, e-commerce customer support, airline, and travel/hotels — threading identities (Tessa Coleman / Nina Patel / Maya Chen) that the user never fully restates. The run breaks into: a retail order edit (T1), a cross-system return requiring heavy skill-scoping workarounds (T2), a policy-grounded refusal of an unfounded travel-certificate request (T3), a flight search and booking paid partly by a $100 certificate (T4–T6), and a long tail of comparisons, hotel bookings (Seattle/Chicago/Las Vegas) and profile/recall restatements (T7–T13), ending in a session summary (T14). The densest turns are T2 (multi-step diagnosis of a user-vs-order skill-scope mismatch) and T3 (recall of the just-processed retail return used to justify declining airline compensation). Every probe turn (T3, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9, T12) is answered from working memory with no re-retrieval, and the agent repeatedly routes around FlightDB.load() validation errors. Recall quality is high (23/27 credited); the visible misses are token-level — not printing the cheapest mouse's product_id (T8) and a certificate/membership-tier token mismatch (T12) — rather than genuine recall failures.
